d: The positive feedback loop of labor in which stretching of the cervix and vagina by the presenting part signals the hypothalamus to release more oxytocin, which strengthens contractions.
A cervical score built from dilation, effacement, station, consistency and position; a score of 8 or more predicts successful induction, and a low score calls for cervical ripening first.
An antepartum test that adds four ultrasound items, fetal breathing, movement, tone and amniotic fluid volume, to the non-stress test, scoring each 0 or 2; 8 to 10 is reassuring.
Upper brachial plexus injury (C5 and C6) from lateral neck traction, often in shoulder dystocia; the arm is adducted and internally rotated with the elbow extended, the waiter's tip.
Failure of the myometrium to contract after delivery, leaving the placental-bed vessels open; it causes most postpartum hemorrhages and is treated first with massage and oxytocin.
Milk ejection triggered by suckling: oxytocin from the posterior pituitary contracts the myoepithelial cells around the breast alveoli, pushing milk into the ducts.
